knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```{r load}
# data from data-raw/vignette_cut_points.R and data-raw/vignette_cut_points_places.R
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "knowledge", mustWork = TRUE)
x <- readRDS(vd("cut_points.rds"))
pl <- readRDS(vd("cut_points_places.rds"))
# the places were measured on this bundle
stopifnot(identical(pl$meta$bundle_md5, unname(tools::md5sum(vd("cut_points.rds")))))
places <- pl$places

# formatting
n0 <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
pc <- function(v, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * v, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
grad <- function(g, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * g, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
lim <- function(g) paste0(signif(100 * g, 3), " %")
link_site <- "https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/link/"
research <- "https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/knowledge/blob/main/research/minimal_network_tuning.md"
where <- function(p) {
  r <- places[places$place == p$place & places$site_visit %in% p$site_visit, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  nm <- if (is.na(r$gnis_name)) "an unnamed stream" else r$gnis_name
  via <- if (r$joins_direct) "flowing into" else "draining to"
  sprintf("%s %s the %s, %s km %s of %s", nm, via, r$joins, n0(r$town_km), r$compass, r$town)
}

# ---- the premise: sites that start a segment of their own ----------------------------------------------------------
pm <- x$premise
pm_at <- function(n, cs) pm$at_site_pct[pm$network == n & pm$catch_status == cs] / 100
stopifnot(nrow(pm) == 6, all(c("published_92", "published_145", "minimal") %in% pm$network))
# the same visits on each network, so the footnote's counts hold for every row
stopifnot(all(tapply(pm$visits, pm$catch_status, function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1)))
# the sentences: on both full networks a site with fish starts its own segment far more often than one without; on
# the minimal network the two are close
stopifnot(pm_at("published_145", "fish") > 5 * pm_at("published_145", "zero"),
          pm_at("published_92", "fish") > 5 * pm_at("published_92", "zero"),
          abs(pm_at("minimal", "fish") - pm_at("minimal", "zero")) < 0.01,
          pm_at("published_145", "fish") / pm_at("published_92", "fish") > 0.4,
          pm_at("published_145", "fish") / pm_at("published_92", "fish") < 0.6)

# ---- the setups --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
su <- x$setups
s_of <- function(s) su[su$setup == s, ]
stopifnot(identical(su$setup, c("published", "minimal", "parent", "atlas")), length(unique(su$n_visits)) == 1)
in_reg <- function(pick_of, region_of) {
  t <- x$tune[[region_of]]
  v <- t$in_region[t$rule == s_of(pick_of)$pick]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  v == "TRUE"
}
# the opening's words: 13 % on the full network, 9 % on the minimal, the 13 % no close call on the minimal network's
# records and the 9 % a close call on the full network's; the parent setup picks the minimal network's rule exactly,
# the Atlas line a steeper limit; every pick keeps the flow floor and the near-a-river allowance
stopifnot(s_of("published")$grad_max == 0.13, s_of("minimal")$grad_max == 0.09,
          !in_reg("published", "minimal"), in_reg("minimal", "published"),
          s_of("parent")$pick == s_of("minimal")$pick, s_of("atlas")$grad_max > s_of("published")$grad_max,
          !in_reg("atlas", "published"), !in_reg("atlas", "minimal"),
          length(unique(sub("\\|g<=[0-9.]+\\|", "|", su$pick))) == 1)
d_on <- as.Date(substr(s_of("published")$tune_run, 1, 8), "%Y%m%d")
# the published setup is the full network reading each segment's own slope
stopifnot(s_of("published")$token_cut == "cut-full-top", s_of("published")$curve_grad == "segment_gradient")
tuned_on <- paste(as.integer(format(d_on, "%d")), format(d_on, "%B %Y"))
# every close call changes all three parts of link's rule, on every setup
stopifnot(all(vapply(x$tune, function(t) all(t$departures[t$in_region == "TRUE"] == "3"), TRUE)))
# rules other than the chosen one with a given limit that are close calls on a setup's records
n_lim <- function(region_of, g) {
  t <- x$tune[[region_of]]
  sum(t$in_region == "TRUE" & as.numeric(t$grad_max) == g & t$rule != s_of("published")$pick)
}
stopifnot(n_lim("minimal", s_of("published")$grad_max) > 0)
tr <- x$transfer
transfer_pct <- tr$minimal_only_km / tr$minimal_km
stopifnot(abs(tr$parent_km - s_of("parent")$tuned_km) < 0.05, transfer_pct < 0.02, tr$parent_only_km < tr$minimal_only_km)

# ---- the other keys ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ok <- x$other_keys
# chinook rearing is reported on its own above, so the sentence counts the others
stopifnot(nrow(ok) == 7, "CH_rear" %in% ok$key[ok$network_moved != "same"])
ok6 <- ok[ok$key != "CH_rear", ]
n_moved <- sum(ok6$network_moved != "same")
n_out <- sum(!ok6$minimal_in_full_region | !ok6$full_in_minimal_region)
stopifnot(nrow(ok6) == 6, n_moved == 3, n_out == 2)

# ---- the sites that change side ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
st <- x$sites
crit <- x$criteria
n_sites <- nrow(st)
n_fish <- sum(st$present)
# the two networks' own slopes (a full segment's minimal parent reads another slope at a few sites); the examples
# below are chosen on the parent's, as the bundle chose them
side <- function(g, t) g <= t
st$cross_m <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(crit$limits, function(t) side(st$full_gradient, t) != side(st$minimal_gradient, t)))
st$d <- st$full_gradient - st$minimal_gradient
cr <- st[st$cross_m, ]
steep <- function(g, present) mean(g[st$present == present] > crit$limits[["minimal"]])
# the tuning's sites: those in groups where chinook were caught at some sites and not others
both_out <- ave(st$present, st$watershed_group_code, FUN = function(p) any(p) && !all(p))
stopifnot(sum(both_out) == su$n_visits[1])
cr_scored <- st[st$cross_m & both_out, ]
stopifnot(sum(cr$present) < 10, sum(cr$d > 0) > 2 * sum(cr$d < 0),
          steep(st$full_gradient, FALSE) > steep(st$minimal_gradient, FALSE),
          steep(st$full_gradient, TRUE) > steep(st$minimal_gradient, TRUE))
```

[`link`](`r link_site`) [@irvine2026linkDevelop], an R package, maps where each fish species can spawn and rear on
British Columbia's streams. It cuts the streams of the BC Freshwater Atlas [@flnrord2021FreshwaterAtlasb] into
segments and tests each segment against a few thresholds, one of them a steepest slope. Some of its cuts fall where
fish were caught, so at a site that caught fish the slope a rule reads is often worked out over a short stretch that
starts at the catch. That can move the thresholds this package tunes from the same catches. On link's full network,
chinook rearing's slope limit is **`r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)`**; on its minimal network, which drops
the cuts at crossings, at hand-mapped habitat and at fish records, it is **`r lim(s_of("minimal")$grad_max)`**, and on the minimal network's records the
full network's rule is not a close call. Read on the full network with each segment taking its
minimal-network slope, the records choose `r lim(s_of("parent")$grad_max)` again.

```{r profile-data}
cc <- x$concept
sg <- cc$segments
xmax <- 700
pr <- cc$atlas_profile[cc$atlas_profile$measure <= xmax + 50, ]
lab_net <- c(full = "Full network", minimal = "Minimal network", atlas = "Atlas line")
cols_net <- c("Full network" = "#d95f02", "Minimal network" = "#1b6ca8", "Atlas line" = "grey40")
sg$net <- factor(lab_net[sg$network], levels = lab_net)
site_seg <- sg[sg$from_m <= cc$site$measure & sg$to_m > cc$site$measure, ]
stopifnot(nrow(site_seg) == 3, setequal(site_seg$network, names(lab_net)))
seg_at <- function(n) site_seg[site_seg$network == n, ]
# the profile's words: the full network cuts at the catch, so the site starts a segment of its own, steeper than its
# minimal segment and gentler than the whole Atlas line
stopifnot(abs(seg_at("full")$from_m - cc$site$measure) < 1, cc$site$present,
          abs(seg_at("full")$gradient - cc$site$full_gradient) < 1e-4,
          abs(seg_at("minimal")$gradient - cc$site$minimal_gradient) < 1e-4,
          seg_at("full")$gradient > crit$limits[["minimal"]], seg_at("minimal")$gradient < crit$limits[["minimal"]],
          seg_at("atlas")$gradient > crit$limits[["published"]], seg_at("minimal")$from_m < 50,
          seg_at("atlas")$z_up > 1040)  # the caption: the Atlas line runs past the top of the figure
cc_sites <- cc$sites
cc_sites$z <- stats::approx(pr$measure, pr$z, cc_sites$measure)$y
site_seg$lab <- sprintf("%s: %s over %s", site_seg$net, grad(site_seg$gradient),
                        ifelse(site_seg$length_metre >= 1000, paste(formatC(site_seg$length_metre / 1000, format = "f", digits = 1), "km"),
                               paste(n0(site_seg$length_metre), "m")))
```

```{r profile, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = paste0("One stream cut two ways: ", where(list(place = "concept", site_visit = cc$site$site_visit)), ". The grey band is the stream's elevation along its Atlas line. Each coloured line is a segment drawn as the straight slope a rule reads on it, with ticks at the ends of the full and minimal networks' segments: orange the full network's, blue the minimal network's, dark grey the whole Atlas line's, which runs on past the top of the figure. The black dot is a site where chinook were caught, the open circle one where none were. The labels give the slope each version reads at the black dot. Elevation is stretched several times so the slopes can be seen.")}
lab_pos <- data.frame(net = site_seg$net, lab = site_seg$lab,
                      x = c(full = 440, minimal = 330, atlas = 300)[site_seg$network],
                      y = c(full = 994.5, minimal = 1016, atlas = 1036)[site_seg$network])
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = pr, aes(measure, z), colour = "grey82", linewidth = 2.4) +
  geom_segment(data = sg, aes(x = from_m, xend = to_m, y = z_dn, yend = z_up, colour = net), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = sg[sg$network != "atlas", ], aes(x = from_m, y = z_dn, colour = net), shape = 124, size = 4,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = cc_sites, aes(measure, z, shape = present), size = 2.6, fill = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_label(data = lab_pos, aes(x, y, label = lab, colour = net), size = 3, hjust = 0, label.size = 0,
             fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols_net, name = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, xmax), ylim = c(990, 1040)) +
  labs(x = "Distance upstream from the stream's mouth (m)", y = "Elevation (m)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## What does a cut do to the slope at a fish site?

A segment's slope is its drop over its length, so where a segment starts and ends decides the slope a rule reads.
Both of link's networks cut a stream where one Atlas line meets the next, at natural barriers and at the steep sections
a species cannot pass. The full network adds cuts the minimal network does not make, among them road and rail
crossings, the ends of stretches whose habitat has been mapped by hand, and records of the species link models in each
watershed group: in the build used here, each such species' highest record on each stream, drawn from bcfishobs
[@norris2024smnorrisbcfishobs].
An electrofishing site that caught fish is often such a record, so the cut lands at the site, and the slope a rule
reads there is worked out from the site upstream. On the stream above, the site that caught chinook reads
`r grad(seg_at("full")$gradient)` on the full network, over the `r n0(seg_at("full")$length_metre)` m above it, and
`r grad(seg_at("minimal")$gradient)` on the minimal network, whose segment runs from near the mouth past the site.

The table counts the electrofishing visits (a site
fished on one occasion) in the Fisheries Data Information System [@provinceofbritishcolumbia2022FisheriesData] that
start a segment of their own, meaning the segment begins within a few metres of the site:

```{r premise}
lab_pm <- c(published_92 = "link 0.66.0, full network (every record of a modelled species a cut)",
            published_145 = "link 0.78.2, full network (each modelled species' highest record on a stream a cut)",
            minimal = "link 0.78.1, minimal network (no crossings, mapped habitat or records)")
tb <- data.frame(Network = unname(lab_pm[c("published_92", "published_145", "minimal")]),
                 `Visits with fish` = pc(c(pm_at("published_92", "fish"), pm_at("published_145", "fish"),
                                          pm_at("minimal", "fish")), 1),
                 `Visits without` = pc(c(pm_at("published_92", "zero"), pm_at("published_145", "zero"),
                                        pm_at("minimal", "zero")), 1),
                 check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tb, format = "html", align = "lrr",
             caption = "Electrofishing visits that start a segment of their own, on three of link's networks.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general_title = "", general = paste0(
    "The same ", n0(sum(pm$visits[pm$network == "minimal"])), " electrofishing visits on each network are those of a ",
    "usual fished area on the stream lines the tuning scores: ", n0(pm$visits[pm$network == "minimal" & pm$catch_status == "fish"]),
    " where fish of any species were caught and ", n0(pm$visits[pm$network == "minimal" & pm$catch_status == "zero"]),
    " where none were. A visit starts its own segment when the segment begins between 1 m below it and 5 m above it."))
```

On both full networks a site that caught fish is far more likely to start a segment of its own than one that caught
none. The newer full network cuts at fewer fish records and halves the share; the minimal network takes the
difference away.

## Where does it bite on our own data?

The tuning for chinook rearing starts from `r n0(n_sites)` of those visits, the ones in chinook's range that pass its
other filters ([which visits](habitat_thresholds.html#lost)), `r n0(n_fish)` of them where chinook were caught. On the full
network, `r pc(steep(st$full_gradient, FALSE))` of the visits without chinook read a slope over
`r lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]])`, against `r pc(steep(st$minimal_gradient, FALSE))` on the minimal network's
segments; at the visits with chinook, `r pc(steep(st$full_gradient, TRUE), 1)` against
`r pc(steep(st$minimal_gradient, TRUE), 1)`. At `r n0(nrow(cr))` visits the two networks put the slope on opposite
sides of `r lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]])` or `r lim(crit$limits[["published"]])`, the two limits the tuning
chose. Only `r sum(cr$present)` of them caught chinook, and at `r n0(sum(cr$d > 0))` the full network reads the
steeper slope. So the full network's cuts move the slope at many more visits than those where chinook were caught;
these runs do not say which of its cuts move them.

```{r strip-data}
cls_lab <- c(paste(lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]]), "or less"),
             paste("over", lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]]), "to", lim(crit$limits[["published"]])),
             paste("over", lim(crit$limits[["published"]])))
cols_cls <- stats::setNames(c("#c6dbef", "#fdae6b", "#d7301f"), cls_lab)
half <- 600
ex <- x$examples
stopifnot(length(ex) == crit$n_examples)
# each example meets the criteria the bundle chose it by: chinook caught, a full segment of at least min_len_m, its
# slope and its minimal parent's on opposite sides of a tuned limit, one per group
for (e in ex) {
  stopifnot(e$site$present, e$site$crosses, e$site$full_length_m >= crit$min_len_m,
            e$site$watershed_group_code != cc$site$watershed_group_code,
            abs(e$site$parent_gradient - e$site$minimal_gradient) < 1e-4,
            e$site$full_length_m < e$site$minimal_length_m)
}
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(ex, function(e) e$site$watershed_group_code, ""))) == length(ex))
ex_lab <- vapply(ex, function(e) {
  w <- where(list(place = "example", site_visit = e$site$site_visit))
  paste0(toupper(substr(w, 1, 1)), substr(w, 2, nchar(w)))
}, "")
strip <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(ex), function(i) {
  e <- ex[[i]]
  s <- sf::st_drop_geometry(e$segments)
  s |> transmute(ex = ex_lab[[i]],
                 net = c(full = "Full network", minimal = "Minimal network")[network],
                 from = downstream_route_measure - e$site$measure, to = from + length_metre, gradient)
}))
strip <- strip |>
  filter(to > -half, from < half) |>
  mutate(at_site = from <= 0 & to > 0,
         from = pmax(from, -half), to = pmin(to, half),
         cls = factor(cut(gradient, c(-Inf, crit$limits[["minimal"]], crit$limits[["published"]], Inf), labels = cls_lab),
                      levels = cls_lab),
         y = ifelse(net == "Full network", 2, 1),
         lab = ifelse(to - from > 90 | at_site, grad(gradient), ""),
         ex = factor(ex, levels = unname(ex_lab)))
# the caption: a bar that stops short of the left edge stops at the stream's mouth
for (e in ex) {
  if (e$site$measure < half) stopifnot(min(e$segments$downstream_route_measure) < 1)
}
# the slope each network reads at the site is the one the site's record holds
for (i in seq_along(ex)) {
  s <- strip[strip$ex %in% ex_lab[[i]] & strip$at_site, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 2,
            abs(s$gradient[s$net == "Full network"] - ex[[i]]$site$full_gradient) < 1e-4,
            abs(s$gradient[s$net == "Minimal network"] - ex[[i]]$site$minimal_gradient) < 1e-4)
}
```

Three of the visits with chinook show it. They were chosen by a rule fixed before drawing: among the visits with
chinook whose full-network slope and its minimal parent's sit on opposite sides of a tuned limit, on a full-network
segment at least `r crit$min_len_m` m long and outside the watershed group of the stream drawn above, the largest gap
between the two in each group, from the `r crit$n_examples` groups with the largest gaps.

```{r strip, fig.height = 4.8, fig.cap = paste0("The segments around three sites where chinook were caught, as each network cuts them, drawn along the stream from ", half, " m below the site to ", half, " m above it (a bar that stops short of the left edge stops at the stream's mouth). Each box is a segment, coloured by the slope a rule reads on it and labelled with it where there is room; the black line is the site. The panel titles name each stream, the river it flows or drains into and the nearest town.")}
ggplot(strip) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = from, xmax = to, ymin = y - 0.38, ymax = y + 0.38, fill = cls), colour = "grey30",
            linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_label(data = function(d) d[nzchar(d$lab), ], aes(x = (from + to) / 2, y = y, label = lab), size = 2.5,
             label.size = 0, label.padding = grid::unit(0.1, "lines"), fill = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = c("Minimal network", "Full network")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols_cls, drop = FALSE, name = "Slope a rule reads") +
  facet_wrap(~ex, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Distance upstream of the site (m)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0))
```

```{r strip-words}
# the paragraph below: two of the three read steeper on the full network; on the third the full segment ends above the
# site, below steeper water that the minimal segment averages in
steeper <- vapply(ex, function(e) e$site$full_gradient > e$site$minimal_gradient, TRUE)
stopifnot(sum(steeper) == 2)
g3 <- ex[[which(!steeper)]]
s3 <- sf::st_drop_geometry(g3$segments)
top3 <- g3$site$full_offset_m + g3$site$full_length_m
above3 <- s3[s3$network == "full" & abs(s3$downstream_route_measure - (g3$site$measure + top3)) < 1, ]
stopifnot(nrow(above3) == 1, above3$gradient > g3$site$minimal_gradient,
          g3$site$minimal_offset_m + g3$site$minimal_length_m > top3 + above3$length_metre / 2)
```

The shorter segment does not always read the steeper slope. On two of the three it does. On the third, the full
network's segment ends `r n0(top3)` m above the site, and the steeper water above it, which the minimal network's
segment averages in, is read on its own.

## What do the rules choose on each network?

The tuning scores each candidate rule by how well it predicts where chinook were caught in watershed groups held out
of the fit; lower is better. A score carries error, so every rule within one standard error of the best is a
**close call**: the records cannot rank the close calls apart. Of the close calls, the tuning chooses the one that
changes link's standard rule least, and among equals the best scorer ([how the tuning works](habitat_thresholds.html)).
For chinook rearing every close call changes all three of the rule's parts on every network and slope below, so the
choice is the best scorer. Two networks disagree only when one network's choice is not a close call on the other's
records.

Chinook rearing was tuned four ways on the same `r n0(su$n_visits[1])` visits (those of the
`r n0(n_sites)` in watershed groups where chinook were caught on some visits and not others), the same modelled flows and the same
species range, so that the segments and the slope a rule reads are the only differences. Two of the four read slopes
from another source on the full network's segments: each segment's **minimal parent**, the minimal-network segment it
lies within, and the whole Atlas line it lies on.

```{r setups}
lab_su <- c(published = "Full network", minimal = "Minimal network",
            parent = "Full network", atlas = "Full network")
lab_gr <- c(published = "its own", minimal = "its own", parent = "its minimal parent's", atlas = "its Atlas line's")
yn <- function(v) ifelse(v, "yes", "no")
tb <- data.frame(Segments = unname(lab_su[su$setup]),
                 `Slope a rule reads` = unname(lab_gr[su$setup]),
                 `Slope limit chosen` = lim(su$grad_max),
                 `A close call on the full network?` = yn(vapply(su$setup, in_reg, TRUE, region_of = "published")),
                 `A close call on the minimal network?` = yn(vapply(su$setup, in_reg, TRUE, region_of = "minimal")),
                 `Rearing habitat (km)` = n0(su$tuned_km),
                 `Against link's rule` = paste0(formatC(su$change_pct, format = "f", digits = 1), " %"),
                 check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tb, format = "html", align = "llrccrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The chinook rearing rule chosen on each network and slope.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 13) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general_title = "", general = paste0(
    "Every rule chosen keeps the same flow floor and the same allowance for small streams near a large river; ",
    "only the slope limit differs. Habitat is each rule run through all of link's steps on the segments it was ",
    "tuned on, over the watershed groups link classified for chinook, and the last column compares it with link's ",
    "standard rule run on the same segments and slopes."))
```

On the full network's own slopes the rule chosen has a `r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)` limit, and that rule is not
a close call on the minimal network's records; the minimal network's rule, with `r lim(s_of("minimal")$grad_max)`, is a
close call on the full network's records too. Given each segment's minimal parent's slope, the full network chooses
the minimal network's rule exactly. The Atlas line's slopes choose a `r lim(s_of("atlas")$grad_max)` limit, in a rule
that is a close call on neither network's records; these runs do not show why. The verdicts are on the rules chosen,
not on a limit alone: on the minimal network's records, `r n_lim("minimal", s_of("published")$grad_max)` other rules
with a `r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)` limit, differing in their flow floor or their allowance near a river, are
close calls.

The network moves other species' rules as well. Tuned on the same flows and range, the full and minimal networks
choose different rules for `r n_moved` of the `r nrow(ok6)` other species and stages both could fit, and for `r n_out` of
them one network's choice is not a close call on the other's records ([the research notes](`r research`), "The full
network on the same flows and range").

## Where does the habitat drawn differ?

```{r map-data}
mp <- x$map
mrow <- places[places$place == "map", ]
d <- mp$drawn
lv <- c("Both rules", paste("Own slope,", lim(s_of("published")$grad_max), "limit only"),
        paste("Minimal parent's slope,", lim(s_of("parent")$grad_max), "limit only"))
d$cls <- factor(dplyr::case_when(d$published & d$parent ~ lv[1], d$published ~ lv[2], d$parent ~ lv[3]), levels = lv)
d <- d[!is.na(d$cls), ]
km_cls <- tapply(d$length_metre, d$cls, sum) / 1000
small <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$cls, function(i) sum(d$length_metre[i][d$stream_order[i] <= 3]) / sum(d$length_metre[i]))
# the words: each rule's own km is mostly on small streams (order 3 or less), the shared habitat under half
stopifnot(km_cls[[2]] > 2 * km_cls[[3]], km_cls[[1]] > 10 * (km_cls[[2]] + km_cls[[3]]),
          small[[2]] > 0.75, small[[3]] > 0.75, small[[1]] < 0.5)
d$lwd <- pmin(pmax(d$stream_order, 1), 6) / 3
# the zoom: of a 15 km grid from the group's south-west corner, the cell holding the most km drawn by one rule and not
# the other, each segment counted whole in the cell holding its centroid
cell <- 15000
bb <- sf::st_bbox(mp$background)
dif <- d[d$cls != lv[1], ]
mid <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(dif)))
key <- paste(floor((mid[, "X"] - bb[["xmin"]]) / cell), floor((mid[, "Y"] - bb[["ymin"]]) / cell))
best <- names(which.max(tapply(dif$length_metre, key, sum)))
ij <- as.numeric(strsplit(best, " ")[[1]])
zoom <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = bb[["xmin"]] + ij[1] * cell, ymin = bb[["ymin"]] + ij[2] * cell,
                      xmax = bb[["xmin"]] + (ij[1] + 1) * cell, ymax = bb[["ymin"]] + (ij[2] + 1) * cell),
                    crs = sf::st_crs(mp$background))
km_zoom <- sum(dif$length_metre[key == best]) / 1000
# each panel is drawn on a canvas of its own box's shape, so tmap pads nothing and the scale bars hold: the group's
# extent as it is, and the cell widened about its centre to the zoom panel's shape
map_w <- 7
zoom_h <- 3.6
widen <- function(b, asp) {
  cx <- (b[["xmin"]] + b[["xmax"]]) / 2
  half_w <- max(b[["xmax"]] - b[["xmin"]], asp * (b[["ymax"]] - b[["ymin"]])) / 2
  half_h <- half_w / asp
  cy <- (b[["ymin"]] + b[["ymax"]]) / 2
  sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - half_w, ymin = cy - half_h, xmax = cx + half_w, ymax = cy + half_h), crs = sf::st_crs(b))
}
zoom_box <- widen(zoom, map_w / zoom_h)
over_h <- map_w * (bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]]) / (bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]])
stopifnot(zoom_box[["xmin"]] <= zoom[["xmin"]], zoom_box[["ymax"]] >= zoom[["ymax"]])
```

In the `r mrow$gnis_name` watershed group, around the `r mrow$joins` `r n0(mrow$town_km)` km `r mrow$compass` of
`r mrow$town`, the two rules a user could run on link's full network draw
`r n0(km_cls[[1]])` km of chinook rearing habitat alike. The rule tuned on each segment's own slope adds
`r n0(km_cls[[2]])` km; the rule tuned on the minimal network and read on each segment's minimal parent adds
`r n0(km_cls[[3]])` km. Most of each difference lies on small streams, of stream order 3 or less
(`r pc(small[[2]])` and `r pc(small[[3]])`), against `r pc(small[[1]])` of the habitat both draw.
The group was chosen before drawing as the one with the most km where the four tunings disagree.

```{r map, fig.height = round(over_h + zoom_h, 2), fig.cap = paste0("Chinook rearing habitat in the ", mrow$gnis_name, " watershed group under two rules run on link's full network. Pale blue: drawn by both. Orange: drawn only by the rule tuned on each segment's own slope (a ", lim(s_of("published")$grad_max), " limit). Dark blue: drawn only by the rule tuned on the minimal network, reading each segment's minimal parent's slope (", lim(s_of("parent")$grad_max), "). Grey: other streams chinook can reach. Lakes of 10 ha or more and river polygons are shaded. The lower panel is the box outlined above, centred on the dashed square: of a ", cell / 1000, " km grid laid from the south-west corner of the upper panel, the cell holding the most km drawn by one rule and not the other, counting each segment in the cell that holds its middle (", n0(km_zoom), " km). Line width follows stream order.")}
reg <- gq::gq_reg_main()
cols_map <- stats::setNames(c("#c6dbef", "#d95f02", "#08519c"), lv)
draw <- function(bbox, scale_km, lwd_add, frame_box = NULL, legend = TRUE, dash_box = NULL) {
  both <- d[d$cls == lv[1], ]
  dd <- d[d$cls != lv[1], ]
  dd$lwd <- dd$lwd + lwd_add
  m <- tmap::tm_shape(mp$background, bbox = bbox) + tmap::tm_lines(col = "grey85", lwd = 0.3) +
    tmap::tm_shape(mp$water) + do.call(tmap::tm_polygons, gq::gq_tmap_style(reg$layers$lake)) +
    tmap::tm_shape(both) + tmap::tm_lines(col = cols_map[[1]], lwd = "lwd",
                                          lwd.scale = tmap::tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 1),
                                          lwd.legend = tmap::tm_legend_hide()) +
    tmap::tm_shape(dd) +
    tmap::tm_lines(col = "cls", col.scale = tmap::tm_scale_categorical(values = cols_map, levels.drop = FALSE),
                   col.legend = if (legend) tmap::tm_legend(title = "Chinook rearing drawn by") else tmap::tm_legend_hide(),
                   lwd = "lwd", lwd.scale = tmap::tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 1.6),
                   lwd.legend = tmap::tm_legend_hide())
  if (!is.null(frame_box)) {
    m <- m + tmap::tm_shape(sf::st_as_sfc(frame_box)) + tmap::tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 1.2)
  }
  if (!is.null(dash_box)) {
    m <- m + tmap::tm_shape(sf::st_as_sfc(dash_box)) + tmap::tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 1, lty = "dashed")
  }
  m + tmap::tm_scalebar(breaks = c(0, scale_km / 2, scale_km), position = tmap::tm_pos_in("right", "bottom")) +
    tmap::tm_layout(frame = TRUE, inner.margins = 0, outer.margins = 0,
                    legend.position = tmap::tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
}
f_over <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
f_zoom <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
tmap::tmap_save(draw(bb, 20, 1.2, zoom_box), f_over, width = map_w, height = over_h, dpi = 150)
tmap::tmap_save(draw(zoom_box, 4, 2, legend = FALSE, dash_box = zoom), f_zoom, width = map_w, height = zoom_h, dpi = 150)
grid::grid.newpage()
lay <- grid::grid.layout(2, 1, heights = grid::unit(c(over_h, zoom_h), "null"))
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = lay))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f_over), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f_zoom), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 2))
```

## What does it mean for someone using the thresholds?

This package's chinook rearing thresholds, tuned on `r tuned_on`, were tuned on link's full network, each segment
reading its own slope, which is how link applies a rule. For chinook rearing the same records choose another rule on another
network or with slopes read another way: its slope limit reads `r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)` on the full network's own slopes,
`r lim(s_of("minimal")$grad_max)` on the minimal network's and `r lim(s_of("atlas")$grad_max)` on the Atlas line's,
while the flow floor and the allowance near large rivers hold on all four.

A rule tuned on the minimal network can still be run on the full one, by giving each full segment its minimal
parent's slope. For chinook rearing it then draws `r n0(tr$parent_km)` km against the `r n0(tr$minimal_km)` km it
draws on the minimal network itself: `r n0(tr$minimal_only_km)` km, `r pc(transfer_pct, 1)`, is drawn on the
minimal network alone. The difference comes from the allowance for small streams near a large river, whose distance
is measured from a segment's downstream end: a long minimal segment that starts near a river counts along its whole
length, while its full-network pieces start farther up ([measured in the research notes](`r research`), "Chinook
rearing on every setup").

## Limits

- Across the province, chinook rearing is the only species and stage tuned on all four of the ways above. The `r nrow(ok6)` others both
  networks could fit were tuned on the two networks' own slopes and, in a separate check, on the Atlas line each visit
  lies on ([the methodology article's limits](habitat_thresholds.html#limits)), but not on the minimal parent's slope
  or on the Atlas line of the segment.
- The minimal network drops the cuts at fish records, at crossings and at the ends of hand-mapped habitat together,
  so these runs cannot say which of the three moved the limit.
- Few visits carry the difference: of the `r n0(su$n_visits[1])` visits the tunings scored, `r n0(nrow(cr_scored))`
  read a slope on opposite sides of a chosen limit on the two networks, and `r sum(cr_scored$present)` of those caught
  chinook. The runs show that the network moves the choice, not which visits move it.
- Slopes taken over a fixed length of stream, which would not depend on where fish were caught, were not tested.

## How was this done?

The numbers were bundled on `r x$meta$written` from the tuning runs and link builds the [research
notes](`r research`) describe (link's full network, run `r x$meta$link_run_full`; its minimal network, run
`r x$meta$link_run_minimal`; and, for the first row of the first table, the evidence from link 0.66.0's earlier full
network). When the bundle was written, the share of visits starting their own segment, the four
tunings' choices and habitat, and the other species' counts were each checked against the logs that report them in
the research notes. The sites are the Fisheries Data Information System's electrofishing records, placed on the Freshwater
Atlas; rules are run through fresh [@irvine2026freshFreshwater] for link. [How the tuning
works](habitat_thresholds.html) describes the records, the candidates and the scoring.
